title: Tanzanian Peanut Brittle
community: The market sweet sold everywhere in Tanzania
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Simsim na Karanga — peanuts and sesame seeds bound together in caramelised sugar into a hard, brittle candy. Sold in small squares at every market across Tanzania — the most universally eaten Tanzanian sweet.
longDesc: Peanut and sesame brittle is Tanzania's most widely sold market sweet — the caramelised sugar binding of roasted peanuts and sesame seeds produces a candy that is simultaneously nutty, sweet, and satisfyingly crunchy. Sold in small squares wrapped in newspaper by vendors at every market.
equipment: Greased baking sheet or marble slab
steps: Toast sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden. Roast groundnuts until fragrant.
Combine sugar and water in a heavy saucepan over medium heat.
Cook without stirring until the sugar reaches 150°C (hard crack stage) — deep amber.
Working quickly, stir in roasted groundnuts, sesame, and salt.
Pour immediately onto a greased surface.
Spread thin with a greased spatula.
Mark into squares while still warm. Break when cool.
chefTips: The sugar must reach hard crack stage — a drop in cold water should snap, not bend.
Work very fast once nuts go in — the sugar sets quickly.
Never stir the sugar while it is cooking — causes crystallisation.
cookingScience: See TZA127 for candy sugar science. Hard crack stage (150—155°C) means virtually all water has evaporated from the sugar solution. At this temperature, the liquid sugar is supersaturated — when combined with the nuts and poured out, it crystallises into a rigid glass-like structure as it cools.
sustainabilityTips: Groundnuts and sesame both locally grown in Tanzania.
healthBenefits: Groundnuts add protein and healthy fats.
culturalNote: Peanut and sesame brittle is Tanzania's most democratic sweet — bought by every Tanzanian, at every market, made by every confectioner in exactly the same way. It is the sweet that crosses every social boundary in the country.
